title: Characterizing spatiotemporal white matter hyperintensity pathophysiology in vivo to disentangle vascular and neurodegenerative contributions.
summary: The paper reports a reproducible posterior WMH signature associated with dementia/Alzheimer disease, consistent with selective fiber degeneration and connections to tau-vulnerable cortex. Discovery cohort UK Biobank n=32,526; signature transferred/reproduced in independent ADNI data. Classification was moderate (mean AUROC 0.706); authors say biological interpretation is tentative and requires histological confirmation.
ai_technology: Voxelwise Bayesian regression normative models normalized seven MRI markers for age/sex; clustering and machine-learning disease models identified spatial signatures.
organization: Cerebral Imaging Centre, Douglas Mental Health University Institute, Montreal, Canada

source_review.scope: Full primary institutional author copy reviewed. Voxel-wise Bayesian linear-regression normative models of seven MRI markers were fitted in UK Biobank (n=32,526), then transferred to ADNI; unsupervised clustering and machine-learning disease modeling identified a reproducible posterior WMH signature associated with dementia/Alzheimer disease. First published online 2026-03-31. Snapshot comparison found no same result; the existing WMH segmentation-tool record is a different claim.
